description:
This project presents a series of compositions featuring Earth and an Ariane 6 rocket. The scene setup and framing were created over the course of a single evening. The Earth asset itself had been completed several months earlier as part of a separate project, while the Ariane 6 model is a 3D asset found online. The model came without textures and, due to time constraints, it was used as-is for these renders.

The Earth asset relies on very high-resolution datasets, with textures available up to 86K resolution (although these were not used here due to GPU limitations). The renders shown here use 43K and 21K textures instead.

A significant part of the work lies in the shader system used to recreate the appearance of Earth’s atmosphere. The setup includes a horizon transition between the planet and space, an atmosphere whose density gradually decreases with altitude, and color variations near sunrise and sunset. The cloud system is volumetric in appearance and produces both self-shadowing and cast shadows. These shadows are visible not only on the surface but also within the atmosphere itself, forming large shadow trails across the cloud layers.

This is the third complete iteration of this Earth asset, rebuilt from scratch roughly four years after the first version. Compared to the previous iteration, this version introduces a different approach for the atmosphere: instead of constructing the effect in Blender’s compositor, the atmospheric density is now handled directly in the shader and varies with altitude.

From a scientific standpoint, the scene was not designed to be physically accurate with respect to the rocket. Elements such as trajectory, launch location, altitude, booster separation, or the exact position of the sun were not considered. The orientation of the Earth, cloud layer, rocket, and light source was adjusted primarily for visual composition. The images should therefore be considered illustrative rather than scientifically accurate.

The scene was created in Blender 4.5. External shots use a 70 mm camera, while the onboard shots attached to the rocket use a 40 mm lens. Rendering was done with Cycles at a resolution of 3840 × 1608 pixels, using 512 samples and a noise threshold of 0.01. The volumetric render step rate was set to 0.01, which strongly affects the appearance of the cloud volumes but increases render times. Each image took approximately 45 minutes to render before being exported in linear Rec. 709 for a quick post-production pass in DaVinci Resolve.

The project was produced on a laptop running Ubuntu, equipped with an NVIDIA RTX 3050 Laptop GPU, 16 GB of RAM, and an Intel i7-12700H processor.
